meta.description: Every scheduled agentic run — morning brief, evening review, weekly digest — in one list instead of one workflow each. Each entry names its own time, days, agent and intent. Unlike the watch templates these DO cost a turn each time they fire, because that is the point: the agent is being asked to go and do the work. Fork per agent or per theme. Safe to activate with an empty list.

nodes.name: Every 5 minutes
nodes.notes:
A 5-minute TICK, not the briefing schedule — each briefing's own time lives in the list below. This is what lets one workflow hold briefings at 08:00, 20:00 and Sunday 19:00 without three separate workflows.

A briefing therefore fires on the first tick at or after its time, i.e. up to 5 minutes late. If you need one to the minute, give it its own workflow with a real cron.

The tick itself costs nothing — it is a Code node deciding 'not yet' 287 times a day.

nodes.name: Briefing list
nodes.notes:
⚙️ EDIT HERE — the whole configuration surface. One block per briefing in the BRIEFINGS array; the comment block documents every field.

A briefing fires once per day: store.fired[id] records the date it last ran, in the workflow's static data, so the remaining ~140 ticks that day return nothing.

CAUTION when testing: clearing that memory (or renaming an id) makes a past-due briefing fire immediately on the next tick, which costs a turn.

TO FORK: duplicate, keep the briefings you want, rename, activate.

nodes.name: Igor: run briefing
nodes.notes:
Runs the briefing as a real, persisted chat turn in the agent's own session — readable afterwards in the app, cancellable, and visible to the next turn in that session.

output_mode 'push' means whatever the agent writes IS the Telegram message; it must not also call send_telegram_message (the seed tells it so).

Retries cover the 503 the trigger endpoint returns when the turn registry is at capacity — without them a briefing lost to a busy moment would simply not happen that day, since the gate has already marked it fired.
